The core conclusion is that different cell lineages and developmental stages are associated with cell-type-specific transcriptional programs. The graph is a multi-gene, multi-lineage, multi-age expression-trajectory panel and is worth 30 points. Understanding the expression source, trajectory categories, and developmental trajectory analysis is worth 20 points. The scientific interpretation is split into three items: glutamatergic marker dynamics 15, GABAergic and glial marker dynamics 15, and the cell-type-specific, time-resolved transcriptional-program conclusion with causal boundary 20. Point allocation: graph reproduction 30, expression source and trajectory categories 20, excitatory marker dynamics 15, GABA/glia marker dynamics 15, transcriptional-program conclusion and boundary 20.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Fig. 4B shows scaled expression trajectories of representative marker genes across cell lineages and developmental ages, including genes associated with pan-glutamatergic, IT glutamatergic, nonIT glutamatergic, GABAergic, and glial populations. Many marker genes show higher expression in their corresponding subclasses and can be assigned to trajectory categories such as Up, Transient Up, Down, or Constant, reflecting sustained increases, transient increases, decreases, or relatively stable temporal patterns. The panel supports the conclusion that cell-fate establishment and maturation in the developing visual cortex involve cell-type-specific and time-resolved transcriptional programs, but these expression trajectories primarily show correlation and do not by themselves prove that any individual gene causally regulates cell fate.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly analyzes and visualizes developmental marker-gene expression trajectories related to Fig. 4B. The reproduced figure should show representative marker genes across developmental ages, preserve scaled or normalized expression information, and communicate trajectory categories such as Up, Transient Up, Down, or Constant. Genes should be organized by major cell-type or lineage groups, such as excitatory/glutamatergic, inhibitory/GABAergic, and glial lineages; finer Pan Glut, IT, NonIT, GABA, and Glia groupings are desirable but not strictly required if the broader lineage organization is clear.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct the full 30 points if the panel is misidentified as a UMAP, single-age heatmap, DE-gene volcano plot, cell-proportion plot, or unrelated analysis. Deduct 10 points if the developmental time axis is missing. Deduct 8-10 points if marker-gene expression values are not shown or are confused with cell counts, subclass proportions, or DE-gene counts. Deduct 6-8 points if trajectory-category information is completely omitted. Deduct 5-8 points if genes are not organized by any meaningful cell-type or lineage category. Do not heavily penalize the use of normalized expression, log-normalized expression, log1p CP10K, heatmaps, or equivalent trajectory visualizations instead of the exact original scaled-expression line-plot layout, as long as temporal marker-gene expression dynamics and major lineage groupings remain interpretable.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains that the plotted values represent scaled or normalized marker-gene expression across developmental ages in scRNA-seq data, and that genes are assigned or compared to developmental trajectory categories such as Up, Transient Up, Down, and Constant, optionally using generalized additive models, clustering, or equivalent trajectory analysis.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points if the curves are interpreted as cell counts, subclass proportions, or DE-gene counts. Deduct 6 points if the response does not indicate that the expression values come from single-cell transcriptomic or scRNA-seq data. Deduct 6 points if scaled, normalized, or log-normalized expression is not explained. Deduct 6 points if developmental trajectory analysis or trajectory categories are completely omitted. Do not deduct solely because expression is shown as normalized or log-normalized expression rather than exactly scaled expression, provided the marker-gene temporal expression interpretation is clear.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the developmental dynamics of marker genes related to pan-glutamatergic, IT glutamatergic, and nonIT glutamatergic populations, including initiation, increase, maintenance, or layer/projection-type-related differential expression in specific excitatory-neuron lineages.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 8 points if glutamatergic marker dynamics are not discussed. Deduct 8 points if excitatory-neuron markers are incorrectly assigned to glial or GABAergic markers. Deduct 6 points if gene names are merely listed without interpreting temporal dynamics.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the dynamic differences among GABAergic and glial marker genes, stating that GABAergic-related genes and glial, oligodendrocyte, or astrocyte-related genes show onset timing, persistence, or stage-specific changes that differ from excitatory-neuron markers.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 8 points if GABAergic or glial marker dynamics are not discussed. Deduct 6 points if GABAergic and glial markers are confused. Deduct 6 points if expression changes are mentioned without explaining lineage specificity.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly states that Fig. 4B supports the involvement of cell-type-specific and time-resolved transcriptional programs in visual-cortex cell-fate establishment and maturation, while avoiding the overinterpretation that expression correlation alone proves causal regulation by individual genes.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points if the response only describes curve changes without stating the cell-type-specific transcriptional-program conclusion. Deduct 10 points if marker-gene expression is directly interpreted as proof of causal regulation. Deduct 6 points if developmental time resolution is not discussed.

Acceptable deviations: It is acceptable to describe scaled expression trajectories as normalized expression trajectories or marker-gene temporal expression curves.
It is acceptable to describe Pan Glut, IT, NonIT, GABA, and Glia as excitatory, inhibitory, and glial lineage categories.
Listing all marker genes is not required as long as excitatory, GABAergic, and glial marker dynamics are summarized.
It is acceptable to abbreviate generalized additive model as GAM or describe it as a developmental trajectory model.
It is acceptable to state the causal boundary as the panel showing expression correlation rather than functional perturbation evidence.
Developmental time may be summarized as E11.5 to P56.
It is acceptable to describe gene trajectory patterns as sustained up, transient up, down, or constant expression categories.
rubric.Scoring instructions: High scores (85-100) require correctly reproducing the multi-panel marker-gene expression trajectories, explaining the expression source, trajectory categories, and trajectory analysis method, separately interpreting glutamatergic, GABAergic, and glial marker dynamics, and extracting the scientific conclusion about cell-type-specific, time-resolved transcriptional programs while preserving the causal interpretation boundary. Partial scores (40-84) should be assigned when the graph structure or some marker dynamics are correct but the expression source, trajectory categories, lineage differences, or scientific meaning is incomplete. Low scores (0-39) should be assigned when the panel is misidentified as a UMAP, proportion plot, or DE plot, or when expression trajectories are overinterpreted as direct proof of causal gene regulation.
